mentions.name: Egregore
mentions.description: Egregore adds a shared cognition layer on top of Claude Code, giving teams shared memory where one person's working session automatically becomes context for the next person's agent session. It lets teams share tooling, knowledge, and skills that evolve with how they work, supports handoffs between team members, structured reflection on workflows, and a knowledge graph that connects decisions to who made them and why. It is terminal-first and git-native, and is looking for early alpha testers.
mentions.problem: Agent memory tools are all single-player: an agent only remembers what you did and has no idea what a co-founder spent hours figuring out, so teams solve the same problems twice or discover decisions only when something breaks. The missing piece was shared memory rather than better individual memory.
mentions.audience: Small teams building with Claude Code
mentions.source_excerpt: Egregore (https://egregore.xyz). multiplayer cognition for Claude Code. been building this with my co-founder at curve labs.
